text: Woke up at six to do chem before school because I keep telling myself mornings are when my brain works. It didn't. I sat there with the 2019 paper and got stuck on the same stoichiometry question for twenty minutes while the sky went from dark blue to grey. Mum had left a note on the fridge saying there's soup in the pot and don't stay up late again. I know she means it nicely but it felt like another reminder that everyone is watching how hard I'm trying. I ate the soup cold standing up and ran for the minibus. 182 days until the DSE and I still can't do moles properly.

Got the mock results back in Chem. 38 out of 80. Everyone compared scores in the corridor like it was a game and I just said I did okay and walked away fast. Ming got 71 and he didn't even revise, or that's what he says. At tutorial class the tutor said anyone below 50 should seriously think about dropping the elective, and I felt my face go hot because I'm pretty sure he looked at me. Dad texted asking how the mock went. I left it on read for an hour, then told him I'll tell him tonight. I don't know why I'm scared of my own dad. He never shouts. He just goes quiet in a way that's worse.

Told them at dinner. Dad didn't say anything for a long time, then said medicine is still possible if I get a tutor for chem every week. Mum said maybe I don't need to aim for medicine, and then they started arguing about it like I wasn't at the table. I went to my room and didn't come out. 我知佢哋係擔心我，但係我真係唔知自己想讀咩。 The only good thing today was Jason's big sister messaging me about moles, and when I explained it to her it suddenly made sense to me too. Maybe I'm not bad at chem. Maybe I'm just tired of being measured by it.
